title: Payment Terms and Late Charges on the Workplace Cafe Management Program
content:
Cafe invoices raised under the Workplace Cafe Management Program fall due the number of days after the invoice date printed against the service model, and a payment is recorded against the single invoice it settles rather than against the contract as a whole. This due-date and per-invoice recording rule remains in force as printed.

**When a late charge may be raised.** A late charge is only raised while the contract stands in mobilizing, active, suspended, or in transition out. A late charge is never raised on a closed contract; the balance on a closed contract is pursued as a closed account instead. This condition is checked against the contract's own status on file before the invoice payment or the late charge is posted, and it governs both the posting of an invoice payment and the posting of a late charge on that contract. Only one late charge is raised per invoice per month, and where an invoice is disputed in writing before the grace days expire, no late charge is raised while the dispute stands open. These conditions remain in force.

**Partial payment — no longer in force.** The basis formerly stated that a payment smaller than the invoiced amount settled that invoice in part, left the remainder outstanding on the same invoice, and never spilled over onto another invoice. That clause is no longer in force, superseded by the current basis.

**Overpayment — no longer in force.** The basis formerly stated that a payment larger than the invoiced amount settled that invoice and left the excess on the contract as a credit applied to the next invoice raised. That clause is no longer in force, superseded by the current basis.

**How a late charge was set — no longer in force.** The basis formerly stated that a late charge could only be raised once the grace days printed against the service model had passed beyond the due date, and that it was the monthly late percentage applied to the amount still outstanding, held to the late charge ceiling printed against the service model. That clause is no longer in force, superseded by the current basis; the grace days, the monthly late percentage, and the late charge ceiling printed against the service model remain figures of record and are not restated here as numbers.

**Credit hold.** Once an invoice is past due by the credit hold threshold printed against the service model, no further ordering or funding is accepted on the contract until the balance is settled. This treatment remains in force.

**Parameters printed per service model.** Each of the six service models of the Workplace Cafe Management Program prints its own payment terms, in calendar days from the invoice date; its own grace days before a late charge may be raised; its own monthly late percentage; its own late charge ceiling; and its own credit hold threshold, in days past due. No single figure is shared across all six service models for any of these.

superseded_clauses: A late charge may only be raised once the grace days printed against the service model have passed beyond the due date, and it is the monthly late percentage applied to the amount still outstanding, held to the late charge ceiling printed against the service model.
A payment smaller than the invoiced amount settles that invoice in part, leaves the remainder outstanding on the same invoice, and never spills over onto another invoice.
A payment larger than the invoiced amount settles that invoice and leaves the excess on the contract as a credit applied to the next invoice raised.
